name: ketchup-exchange-comparison
title: v2ecoli baseline central-carbon exchange phenotype vs KETCHUP kinetic models
question:
Does the v2ecoli baseline central-carbon exchange / byproduct phenotype
(glucose, O2, CO2, acetate, NH3, SO4) match the KETCHUP core-metabolism
kinetic models k-ecoli74 and k-ecoli307, when both are glucose-normalized and
graded by the report-card flux_scatter criterion?

report.title: ketchup-exchange-comparison — v2ecoli baseline vs KETCHUP k-ecoli74/307 + Millard 2017
report.evidence_quality: multi-axis report cards (whole-vector R^2 + per-metabolite rel-tol) over 3 kinetic models
report.objective:
Grade the v2ecoli whole-cell baseline central-carbon exchange-flux vector
against THREE kinetic models (used as report-card reference sources) —
KETCHUP k-ecoli74, KETCHUP k-ecoli307, and the Millard 2017 central-carbon
ODE — to characterize which kinetic regime v2ecoli's baseline byproduct
partitioning resembles. A CHARACTERIZATION, not a v2ecoli pass/fail.
report.setup:
MEASURED = v2ecoli baseline exchange fluxes (pinned population_phenotype_basal
reference, 20-seed ensemble mean), glucose-normalized to -100. REFERENCES =
(1) KETCHUP k-ecoli74 / k-ecoli307 fitted exchange fluxes (pbg-ketchup
KetchupEstimator, boundary reactions → EcoCyc IDs); (2) the Millard 2017 ODE
(millard2017_metabolism / COPASI, the flux source of millard_fba_bridge_harness;
glucose + acetate only). Each model graded by report_card.py with a
whole-vector flux_scatter axis PLUS per-metabolite rel_tol axes (O2/CO2/NH3).
report.finding:
v2ecoli's baseline phenotype lines up with a GLUCOSE-LIMITED kinetic model,
not the batch-aerobic MFA cores — and pinning v2ecoli's central-carbon FBA to
the Millard ODE (the FBA-bridge) moves it PART of the way toward the kinetic
cores' respiration without flipping it into acetate overflow.
  • Millard 2017 ODE — WITHIN_TOL (R^2 = 1.00): both v2ecoli and Millard run
    glucose-limited with NO acetate overflow. (Narrow: Millard exchanges only
    glucose + acetate.)
  • KETCHUP k-ecoli74 / k-ecoli307 — MISMATCH (R^2 = -0.89 / -0.72): directions
    agree (uptake −, CO2 secretion +) but per 100 glucose the cores respire
    far harder (O2 ≈ -135 vs v2ecoli -9; CO2 ≈ +144 vs +33) and secrete acetate
    (≈ +71, absent in v2ecoli → 'lost'). Per-metabolite axes confirm: O2 and
    CO2 mismatch, NH3 drift.
  • v2ecoli + Millard FBA-bridge (millard_fba_bridge_harness) — MISMATCH but
    the CLOSEST candidate (R^2 = +0.65, vs the cores' NEGATIVE R^2; 3 matched,
    1 appeared, 1 lost). The live whole-cell run (viable: dry_mass 380→385 fg
    over the window) respires ~3× the bare baseline (O2 ≈ -26 vs -9 per 100
    glucose) — toward, but still far below, the cores' -135 — while keeping the
    baseline's acetate-free, CO2-quiet signature. So the Millard pin nudges
    respiration up without inducing overflow.
  • KETCHUP FDH dynamic — shown as a NADH(t) data-vs-fit figure (real IPOPT
    time-series fit, optimal, SSE 0.011 over 9 conditions). Not an exchange
    model, so not graded on the scatter axis.
The two KETCHUP models agree closely with each other (shared K-FIT lineage).
Caveat flagged for review: v2ecoli's baseline O2:glucose is anomalously low
(~0.09), which drives much of the magnitude divergence.

assumptions.text:
The pinned population_phenotype_basal reference (20-seed baseline ensemble
mean) is a faithful stand-in for the v2ecoli baseline exchange phenotype, so
no new sim is run for the measured side.

The KETCHUP boundary reactions (up_glc/out_co2/out_ac/up_o2/up_nh3/up_so4
for k-ecoli74; gluc_up/EX_* for k-ecoli307) map 1:1 to the v2ecoli EcoCyc
exchange compound IDs (GLC[p], CARBON-DIOXIDE[p], ACET[p],
OXYGEN-MOLECULE[p], AMMONIUM[c], SULFATE[p]).

model_settings.name: v2ecoli-baseline-reference
model_settings.detail: The MEASURED model: v2ecoli whole-cell baseline. Now also a runnable dashboard variant (v2ecoli-baseline, off a built ParCa cache at out/cache). The report-card MEASURED vector still uses the pinned population_phenotype_basal reference (20-seed ensemble mean) — a better estimate than a short fresh single-cell run.

model_settings.name: ketchup-k-ecoli74-reference
model_settings.detail: KETCHUP k-ecoli74 (108-reaction core) reference source; fitted exchange fluxes from pbg-ketchup (github.com/vivarium-collective/pbg-ketchup).

model_settings.name: ketchup-k-ecoli307-reference
model_settings.detail: KETCHUP k-ecoli307 (305-reaction) reference source; fitted exchange fluxes from pbg-ketchup.

model_settings.name: millard2017-reference
model_settings.detail: Millard 2017 central-carbon ODE (millard2017_metabolism, COPASI) — the flux source of millard_fba_bridge_harness. Covers glucose + acetate only (no O2/CO2/NH3/SO4 exchange).

model_settings.name: fba-bridge-reference
model_settings.detail: v2ecoli + Millard FBA-bridge (millard_fba_bridge_harness): the REAL whole-cell tFBA with the Millard 2017 ODE wired in as a flux source that pins the central-carbon FBA reactions (fba-flux-coupler). Now RUN LIVE off the ParCa cache (60 ticks, viable: dry_mass 380→385 fg); the exchange vector is the time-averaged listeners.fba_results.external_exchange_fluxes (scripts/run_ketchup_models.py bridge). Graded vs the v2ecoli baseline: R^2 = +0.65 — the closest candidate (the bare cores score NEGATIVE R^2).

model_settings.name: ketchup-fdh-dynamic-figure
model_settings.detail: KETCHUP FDH dynamic (KetchupDynamicEstimator): a real IPOPT time-series fit of cell-free formate-dehydrogenase NADH(t) across 9 conditions (optimal, SSE 0.011, 7 params). Shown as a data-vs-fit small-multiples figure (fdh-dynamic.html) — a dynamic kinetic fit has no central-carbon exchange vector, so it is not graded on the scatter axis.

model_settings.name: glucose-normalized-multiaxis-cards
model_settings.detail: All models glucose-normalized to -100; graded by report_card.py with a whole-vector flux_scatter axis (identity-line R^2) PLUS per-metabolite rel_tol axes (O2/CO2/NH3, 30% tol).

runs.name: ketchup-exchange-comparison-grade
runs.description:
Graded the v2ecoli baseline central-carbon exchange vector against four
kinetic models with the PR #134 report-card flux_scatter criterion: the two
KETCHUP cores (k-ecoli74 / k-ecoli307), the Millard 2017 ODE, and the live
v2ecoli + Millard FBA-bridge run. KETCHUP fluxes from pbg-ketchup
(KetchupEstimator, boundary reactions mapped to EcoCyc IDs, glucose-normalized);
the FBA-bridge vector from a live millard_fba_bridge_harness run
(scripts/run_ketchup_models.py bridge); v2ecoli side from the pinned
population_phenotype_basal reference. Built by
scripts/ketchup_baseline_report_cards.py; cards in
docs/report_cards/ketchup_vs_baseline/ (mirrored to
reports/figures/ketchup-exchange-comparison/ for report embedding).

v2ecoli-baseline-matches-ketchup-k-ecoli.detail: Report card: MISMATCH (whole-vector R^2 = -0.89, 4 matched + 2 lost [acetate, SO4]; per-metabolite O2/CO2 mismatch). Directions agree but v2ecoli respires far less per glucose (O2 -9 vs -135, CO2 +33 vs +144) and secretes no acetate (KETCHUP +71). PARTIAL = directionally consistent, quantitatively divergent — expected whole-cell-FBA vs batch-MFA core divergence.

Report card: MISMATCH (whole-vector R^2 = -0.72; same pattern as k-ecoli74, the two KETCHUP models agree closely). NH3 closer here (v2ecoli -136 vs -81). Directions consistent, magnitudes + acetate overflow diverge.

v2ecoli-baseline-matches-millard2017-exc.detail: Report card: WITHIN_TOL (R^2 = 1.00 over the 1 active shared exchange). v2ecoli's baseline AGREES with the Millard 2017 ODE: both glucose-limited with NO acetate overflow. Millard exchanges only glucose + acetate (no O2/CO2/NH3/SO4), so the match is narrow but directionally and qualitatively clean — v2ecoli's phenotype lines up with a glucose-limited kinetic model, not the batch-aerobic KETCHUP cores.

v2ecoli-baseline-matches-fba-bridge-exch.detail: Report card: MISMATCH but the CLOSEST candidate (whole-vector R^2 = +0.65 — POSITIVE, vs the bare cores' negative R^2; 3 matched, 1 appeared, 1 lost). Pinning v2ecoli's central-carbon FBA to the Millard ODE deepens respiration ~3× (O2 ≈ -26 vs baseline -9 per 100 glucose, toward but well below the cores' -135) while keeping the baseline's acetate-free, CO2-quiet exchange signature. Live whole-cell run, viable (dry_mass 380→385 fg over 60 ticks).

runs.name: ketchup-fba-bridge-run
runs.description: Live v2ecoli + Millard FBA-bridge run: the real whole-cell tFBA (~55 procs) with the Millard 2017 ODE wired in as a flux source pinning the central-carbon FBA reactions. 60 1-second ticks off the ParCa cache (out/cache), viable (dry_mass 380→385 fg). Exchange phenotype = time-averaged listeners.fba_results.external_exchange_fluxes (post 10-tick burn-in). Run via scripts/run_ketchup_models.py bridge.
